data.title: Tesla App Adds Passkey Support With Update 4.61.0: Here’s How To Set It Up
data.description:
Tesla has added another layer of account security with the release of mobile app, introducing support for passkeys and giving owners a new way to sign in without relying on a traditional password.

The addition was not in the release notes, but was discovered by X user Rhys Samson (@samsonusmc), who shared a screenshot of the new Passkey option appearing under Tesla’s Sign In Management settings.

The feature is now available to Tesla owners after updating to app version 4.61.0, which was released on the iOS App Store on Friday evening.

What Is A Passkey And Why Is It Important?

A passkey is a modern authentication method that allows users to sign in to their accounts using the same method they use to unlock their devices, such as Face ID, Touch ID, fingerprint recognition, or a device PIN.

Unlike traditional passwords, passkeys use cryptographic credentials rather than a password that must be remembered or entered manually.

This makes them more resistant to phishing attacks, since a passkey is tied to the legitimate website or service and cannot simply be entered into a fraudulent login page.

How To Set Up A Passkey In The Tesla App

Setting up a passkey takes just a few steps:

  1. Open the Tesla app and tap the hamburger (three line) menu in the top-right corner.
  2. Tap your profile name and select Security & Privacy.
  3. Select Sign In Management.
  4. Tap Passkey.
  5. Tap Add Passkey and follow the onscreen instructions.

Once configured, the Sign In Management page will display Passkey: Enabled.

The new feature joins Tesla’s existing security options, including multi-factor authentication, giving owners another way to protect their accounts as more vehicle features and services become accessible through the mobile app.

data.title: SpaceX Restricts Airspace Over McGregor Facility Ahead of Tesla Roadster Event
data.description:
A new FAA temporary flight restriction (TFR) has been issued for space over SpaceX’s McGregor, Texas test facility. The restriction is now in place ahead of Tesla’s upcoming Roadster event near Waco.

The restriction, identified as FAA NOTAM FDC 6/3825, became active on September 18 and remains in place until October 2 at 1200 UTC. It covers a 1.5 nautical mile radius around the Waco VORTAC area, extending from the surface up to 10,000 feet above ground level.

The FAA listed the reason for the restriction as hazards under 14 CFR 91.137(a)(3), which temporarily limits aircraft operations in the affected area.

The NOTAM states, “No pilots may operate an aircraft in the areas covered by this NOTAM.” The listed contact for the restriction is the Fort Worth Air Route Traffic Control Center.

The restricted area is positioned over SpaceX’s Rocket Development and Test Facility near West US Highway 84 and FM 2671 in McGregor, where the company tests rocket engines and other hardware.

The timing makes it likely the restriction is linked to Tesla’s planned October 1 Roadster event, which has been teased with the phrase “Go for launch.”

Tesla has previously shared details about the next-generation Roadster, including plans for a SpaceX-inspired thruster package that the company says will improve performance. The vehicle has faced multiple delays, with Tesla continuing development after earlier launch timelines shifted.

data.title: Tesla Supercharger Site Maps now available in mobile app
data.description:
Tesla has expanded its Supercharger Site Maps feature beyond its in-car navigation, with the feature now available in the mobile app.

The new functionality is included in Tesla app version 4.61.0 and makes it easier for owners to check charging station layouts and live stall availability before arriving at a location.

Accessing Site Maps in the app is simple. Owners can open the charging map and zoom in on a supported Supercharger location. As you get closer, the standard map automatically transitions into a detailed Site Map, showing the layout of the station and individual charging stalls.

The maps display real-time availability, allowing drivers to see which chargers are occupied, available, or out of service without having to be inside their vehicle.

Tesla has also improved the accuracy of its availability information to account for non-Tesla EVs using the network. Vehicles with charge ports in different locations can sometimes block adjacent stalls when using Tesla’s shorter charging cables. Site Maps account for these situations to provide a more accurate picture of which chargers are actually usable.

The addition of Site Maps to the mobile app means owners of older Tesla vehicles equipped with Intel-based infotainment systems can now access the feature. Previously, the Site Maps were limited to newer vehicles with AMD Ryzen processors, leaving many longtime Tesla owners without access.

Tesla first introduced Site Maps as part of its 2025 holiday software update, initially launching at just 18 locations. The feature has since expanded to thousands of sites, with hundreds being added weekly. Supercharger Site Maps arrived in Canada in May.

data.title: Canada’s first Tesla Semi Megachargers to begin construction next month in B.C.
data.description:
A British Columbia trucking company is preparing to become one of Canada’s first Tesla Semi fleet operators, with 12 electric trucks expected to arrive next year. While they may not be the first Canadian company to take delivery of a Tesla Semi, they will become the first in the country to install Tesla’s Megachargers.

According to a report by Electric Autonomy, R.R. Plett Trucking will begin installing the 1.2 MW chargers next month at its headquarters in Langley, along with another facility in Kamloops. That should give the company plenty of time to complete construction before its fleet of 12 Tesla Semis are delivered in June 2027.

BC Hydro is involved in the project to provide the necessary electrical capacity, and the company eventually plans to make the chargers available to other fleets.

For R.R. Plett, the dozen Tesla Semi’s won’t be its first foray into electric trucking, with the company already operating eight Volvo VNR electric trucks on routes serving the Port of Vancouver.

However, the Semi’s range and weight advantages are expected to open up additional routes. The Standard Range Semi offers 523 km (325 miles) of range, compared to the 300–350 km the company currently gets from its Volvo trucks.

The new charging infrastructure will also allow R.R. Plett to operate its electric trucks more frequently.

“You can cut charging time from three hours [with DC fast charging] down to 30 minutes with the [Megachargers], which will help us double shift those trucks,” Plett explained.

R.R. Plett has big electrification plans and aims to establish an electric trucking corridor between Vancouver and Calgary, with additional charging locations being considered in Golden and Calgary.

The announcement comes just days before Tesla’s September 24 inauguration of its new high-volume Semi factory in Sparks, Nevada, which is designed to eventually produce approximately 50,000 trucks annually.

data.title: Tesla Roadster reservations reopen in Canada and the U.S.
data.description:
Tesla has reopened reservations for the next-generation Roadster in Canada and the United States, just under two weeks before the vehicle is finally revealed almost 10 years after its first debut.

According to Tesla’s website, the reservation process has returned with a two-step payment structure. Buyers in Canada must first submit a $6,000 credit card payment, which Tesla lists as “Fully refundable,” followed by a $58,000 wire transfer due within 10 days.

In the U.S. the amounts are $5,000 for the intial deposit, and then $45,000 within 10 days.

Previously, Tesla required US$250,000 to reserve a Founder Series Roadster, before removing pricing from their website in 2021.

Today, Tesla also reminds customers that, “Reservations are not final until the wire transfer payment is received.”

Despite re-opening reservations, Tesla has not provided additional details on delivery dates or final pricing, only saying the purchase price won’t be set until the company figures out what the Roadster will come with in terms of available options and hardware specifications.

The Roadster reservation system returning comes ahead of Tesla’s planned next-generation Roadster reveal on October 1, 2026. The company has also previously indicated the vehicle will be built in Texas, although Tesla has not announced production timing.

data.title: Tesla Semi Production Version Gets Faster, More Efficient as New Factory Details Emerge
data.description:
Tesla has revealed new details about the production version of the Semi, including some impressive acceleration figures and several changes aimed at improving efficiency and simplifying manufacturing.

The information comes thanks to Top Gear, who recently got a behind-the-scenes look at the factory in Nevada. Tesla says the Semi can accelerate from 0-60 mph in just 12.5 seconds without a trailer. Even with a fully loaded trailer, the electric Class 8 truck can reach 60 mph in 24 seconds.

For comparison, a conventional diesel semi can take around 60 seconds to reach the same speed when fully loaded.

One of the more interesting details is that Tesla doesn’t actually paint the Semi. Instead, its body panels are powder coated, similar to Tesla’s Megapack energy storage systems. Eliminating a traditional paint shop reduces the amount of factory space required while also lowering production costs. The Semi will initially be offered in white, with additional colours planned for fleet customers.

Tesla has also managed to make the production Semi about 3% more efficient than earlier prototypes. Changes include a new opening in the front bumper to improve airflow and a redesigned, squarer battery pack that retains heat better in cold weather.

The Standard Range Semi uses a 548 kWh battery pack, while Tesla says the truck is only around seven times less efficient than a Model Y despite its substantially larger size and weight. Its aerodynamics also reportedly beat those of the Bugatti Chiron.

Other production changes include a three-piece front bumper that should make repairs easier and cheaper.

Inside, the Semi retains its distinctive centre-mounted driving position. The cloth seats are both heated and ventilated, while the cab has enough headroom for a 6-foot-6 person to stand upright.

With production now underway in Nevada, the latest details provide a clearer picture of how Tesla has refined the Semi for high-volume manufacturing and real-world fleet use.

data.title: Tesla and SpaceX Take Terafab Trademark Fight to Federal Court
data.description:
Tesla, SpaceX and xAI have taken their dispute over the Terafab trademark to federal court after settlement discussions with semiconductor equipment company TERA-print failed.

The companies filed a declaratory judgment lawsuit this week in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas, asking a judge to rule that their use of the Terafab name does not infringe TERA-print LLC’s existing “Tera-Fab” trademark.

The dispute began in May shortly after Tesla and its partners revealed plans for Terafab, a massive semiconductor manufacturing project in Texas aimed at producing chips for artificial intelligence applications.

Tesla filed three U.S. trademark applications on May 18 for “Terafab” and “Tesla Terafab,” covering semiconductor chips and related manufacturing services. TERA-print, which has held the “Tera-Fab” trademark since 2021 for its desktop photolithography equipment used by researchers, filed an expanded trademark application on May 22 covering areas including semiconductor materials, silicon chips, nanoelectronic devices and AI design services.

The following day, TERA-print sent a cease-and-desist letter to Tesla, according to court documents. The company later threatened legal action on June 10, alleging trademark infringement, false designation and unfair competition.

Both sides participated in six settlement meetings between June and August, but those discussions ultimately failed, leading Tesla, SpaceX and xAI to seek a court ruling.

Tesla and SpaceX argue there is little chance of consumer confusion between the two products. The companies say their Terafab project is planned as a roughly $16.8 billion semiconductor complex spanning about 100 million square feet in Grimes County, Texas, while TERA-print’s product is a tabletop laboratory printer.

TERA-print CTO Andrey Ivankin told PCMag the company feels it was misled during the discussions and intends to defend its trademark. He also noted the company holds a U.S. Department of Defense contract and partially owns Mattiq Inc.

The trademark case will now move forward in federal court as Tesla continue development of the large-scale chip manufacturing facility.

data.title: Tesla FSD Records Nearly 10 Times Fewer Crashes in Belgium
data.description:
Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) has recorded a significantly lower collision rate than human-driven Teslas since the system was approved in Belgium this summer, according to new figures presented to the Flemish Parliament.

Flemish Mobility Minister Annick De Ridder shared the results on Thursday. The data, supplied by Tesla as part of the conditions attached to its Belgian approval, covers driving between June 11 and August 31.

Over that period, Tesla vehicles travelled 24.6 million km with FSD engaged. The largest difference was recorded away from highways, where there was one collision across 9.5 million km of assisted driving.

By comparison, manually driven Teslas were involved in 150 collisions over 146.9 million km. Based on those figures, the collision risk was approximately 9.6 times lower when FSD was active.

The difference was smaller on highways but still favoured Tesla’s driver-assistance technology. Four incidents occurred during 15.1 million km with FSD engaged, compared with 32 incidents across 95.1 million km under manual control. That works out to an improvement of roughly 30 percent.

Five accidents involving participating vehicles were reported to the Flemish administration. FSD was inactive in one, although the driver had disengaged it prematurely while exiting a roundabout. Investigators reportedly found no link between FSD and the other four accidents – all were minor, low-speed collisions without injuries. (via HLN)

Tesla’s data also showed 93 percent fewer automatic emergency braking activations and between 82 and 90 percent fewer abrupt manoeuvres, including hard braking and sharp steering inputs.

The figures add to Tesla’s growing European dataset, which was made public earlier this month, as regulators prepare for a broader EU decision on the technology on October 6.

“New technology deserves critical follow-up, but if the data shows that it can make our roads safer, we must also dare to use that potential,” De Ridder said. “It turns out that road safety and innovation can go hand in hand.”

Before receiving approval in June, Tesla completed 5,000 km of testing on Belgian roads in roughly one month. The testing evaluated how FSD responds to infrastructure and driving conditions specific to Belgium, including tram networks, bicycle streets, advisory bike lanes, supplemental signage, and temporary traffic controls in construction zones.

FSD is already approved in five European countries – the Netherlands, Denmark, Belgium, Estonia, and Lithuania – where more than 70,000 customers are using it for over one million km each day.

data.title: Tesla Optimus Factory Build Accelerates Ahead Of 2027 Production Target
data.description:
New drone footage from Giga Texas shows Tesla’s dedicated Optimus factory taking shape, with the building’s steel structure nearing completion as construction continues on the company’s massive North Campus expansion.

Drone operator Joe Tegtmeyer shared updated aerial views of the site on September 17, showing the Optimus building’s steel frame approaching the final stages of assembly. According to Teslarati, the structure is now roughly five column grids away from reaching the north perimeter beam.

Concrete work is also progressing, with three upper floors already poured while crews continue installing rebar and completing footing and grade-beam work below.

Tesla broke ground on the dedicated Optimus facility in late March, with the first steel installed in May after the company confirmed construction was underway. The building is part of a larger expansion of more than 5.2 million square feet on the north side of the Texas factory campus.

The future Optimus facility is expected to stretch more than 4,000 feet alongside the existing vehicle factory, although it will be narrower in design.

Tesla has previously outlined ambitious plans for Optimus, with CEO Elon Musk targeting eventual production capacity of up to 10 million units annually at full scale. A separate pilot production line at Fremont has reportedly been producing Gen 3 Optimus units since January, with output focused on collecting real-world data ahead of future larger-scale manufacturing.

As we reported earlier this year, Tesla’s Texas Optimus facility is being built alongside other major projects, including the company’s planned Terafab chip manufacturing operation with SpaceX. The co-location is intended to bring key parts of Tesla’s future AI and robotics supply chain closer together.

Tesla has not announced production has started at the Texas Optimus factory. The company’s previously stated timeline targets high-volume Optimus production at Giga Texas in summer 2027, once construction and additional manufacturing infrastructure are complete.

data.title: IMC Logistics adds 50 Tesla Semis to California fleet
data.description:
Tesla has landed another significant Semi order, with IMC Logistics announcing plans to add 50 of the electric Class 8 trucks to its fleet in California.

IMC Logistics describes itself as the largest asset-based marine drayage operator in North America, with more than 2,700 trucks and over 50 locations across the continent. The company confirmed the Tesla Semi deployment this week during the 2026 Intermodal EXPO in Long Beach, where it already had one of its trucks on display.

The order will include a mix of Standard and Long Range Tesla Semis. IMC plans to use the Standard Range version, with a range of 325 miles (523 km) for drayage operations within California, while the Long Range trucks will travel between Southern California and destinations farther inland with its range of up to 500 miles (804 km).

The company did not announce how many of each variant it purchased.

The Tesla Semis won’t be IMC’s first alternative-fuel trucks. The company already operates battery-electric and hydrogen fuel-cell trucks in California, along with trucks powered by renewable diesel. IMC says using several technologies allows it to match different trucks with specific routes and customer requirements.

“We are focused on making sustainability attainable in day-to-day drayage operations,” said Jim Gillis, Pacific Region President at IMC Logistics. “That means taking a blended approach rather than relying on a single technology. The addition of 50 Tesla Semis strengthens that strategy as well as allows IMC to establish zero-emission service for long haul lanes.”

The deal adds to a growing order book for the Tesla Semi as the company ramps up production at its new high-volume factory in Nevada.

Earlier this year, WattEV announced an order for 370 Tesla Semis in a deal worth nearly US$100 million. That record was recently surpassed by Swedish transport company Einride, which last month announced plans to purchase 500 Tesla Semis for its U.S. operations.

Tesla is also preparing to expand the Semi beyond North America. The company recently unveiled its European version of the truck, which offers up to 550 km (342 miles) of range, ahead of planned European deliveries in 2027.
